text:
katie: FYI noticed p95 drift on several customer routes after yesterday's kernel pin roll. p95 up from ~160ms to ~280ms on tier-2 traffic.

arjun: ugh, saw that too. initial suspicion: batching window growth + token budgets being too permissive for medium-length prompts.

lee: attaching quick flamegraph from canary node (snippet):
```
Flamegraph: kernel_select -> batch_builder -> kv_cache_lookup -> attention_kernel
hot path: kv_cache_lookup spikes when batch size > 6
```

maria: perf-bot posted regression alert: `regression: +72ms p95 on route /chat/conv` at 2026-03-17T14:02:00Z :warning:

perf-bot: automated profiling: avg_batch_size increased 24% during peak, kv_hit_ratio dropped 6pp for route-tier: medium.

katie: hypothesis: dynamic token budget inference allowed long-tail requests to hog batch formation, pushing smaller requests into later microbatches -> longer queue latency.

arjun: agree. propose two quick experiments:
1) cap per-request token_budget to route-tier ceiling (e.g., 256 -> 128) for medium tier.
2) change queue policy to prefer microbatching by request_count threshold over token budget when estimated latency > SLO.

lee: I ran a local sim with capped token_budget=128 and queue_policy=prefer_count. results: p95 reduced from 280ms -> 185ms, tail (99) improved from 850ms -> 520ms. KV hit % recovered ~+3pp.

maria: can you paste the config you used?

lee: config snippet:
```
batcher:
  route_tiers:
    medium:
      token_budget_max: 128
      queue_policy: prefer_count
      max_microbatch_size: 6
      slo_ms: 200
```

katie: nice. what about kernel selection? earlier rollout pinned a new attention kernel that is slightly faster at large seq but regresses for small seq. might explain med-tier pain.

arjun: right — kernel_profile shows new_kernel is +12% for seq <=128 under microbatch sizes <=4. fallback to old_kernel for batches where avg_seq < 150 looks promising.

maria: can we implement a cheap heuristic: kernel_selector: if avg_seq_per_batch < 140 AND batch_size <= 6 -> use old_kernel else new_kernel?

lee: I prototyped that and ran AB in staging: combined token_budget cap + kernel_selector gave p95 170ms and CPU/GPU utilization stayed within limits.

perf-bot: AB results summary: control p95=280ms, experiment p95=170ms, request_count throughput +1.6%, cost delta -0.8%.

katie: next steps:
- roll token_budget cap + queue_policy prefer_count to canary 10% for medium tier tonight.
- add kernel_selector fallback rule as config flag (off by default).
- monitor kv_hit_ratio and latency SLOs for 3 hours, auto-rollback threshold p95 > 220ms.

arjun: I'll open a short PR with the config and a unit test for kernel_selector logic. tagging @lee for perf numbers.

lee: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/824 (draft) — includes microbench and sim harness results.

maria: add alert adjustment: when we cap token_budget we expect increased request_count; keep token-cost alert but relax by 5% for the canary window.

katie: one more thing — KV prefetch policy. when we reduce token_budget smaller prefix caching becomes more effective. consider lowering prefetch_stride from 64->32 for medium tier as an optimization. could push kv_hit +2-4pp.

arjun: let's keep prefetch_stride change in the follow-up after canary success. want to isolate variables.

perf-bot: canary deploy scheduled: 2026-03-17T23:00Z -> rolling 10% medium-tier. will post results summary. :rocket:

deploy-bot: canary started (deploy id: d-2026-03-17-23-00).

maria: thanks all. if we see any customer-facing errors or p95 > 220ms we rollback immediately.

katie: leaving checklist in the PR. will update after the 3hr window. :thumbsup:
